TITLE: Investigating Consistency Models on Riemannian Manifolds: A Pilot Study with Protein Backbone Torsion Angle Generation
PROPOSAL: We propose a pilot experiment using a simplified Riemannian manifold for protein backbone torsion angle generation, incorporating a known flow-matching model (e.g., DDPM) [1] and a consistency model variant for the manifold (consistency training with stop-gradient operation on the manifold's vector field).

TITLE: Discrete-Time Consistency Training on Riemannian Manifolds
PROPOSAL: Develop a discrete-time consistency training objective for consistency models on Riemannian manifolds. This objective should be designed to enforce consistency along the probability flow, incorporate manifold constraints, and compute intrinsic distances between predictions on the manifold. The proposed objective can be tested on protein backbone torsion angle generation and RNA torsion angle generation.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Consistency training on Euclidean space; Ablation: compare performance with and without the stop-gradient operation; Manifold-specific baseline: Flow-based models on Riemannian manifolds.
COST: 150 GPU-hours

The stop-gradient operation is crucial for retaining the manifold constraints.

* RNA torsion angle generation:
  + Use a combination of in vitro RNA data and RNA structure predictions [2] as the synthetic data to train the model.
  + Evaluate the model's performance using the MAE and average position root mean square deviation (APRMSD) metrics.
